content.content:
# How this reference app was made

Generated from the original project's own archetype (r7's pinned snapshot):

    mvn archetype:generate -DarchetypeCatalog=local \
        -DarchetypeGroupId=de.terrestris -DarchetypeArtifactId=shogun-core-webapp-archetype \
        -DarchetypeVersion=5.3.14-SNAPSHOT -DgroupId=de.example -DartifactId=shogunref \
        -Dversion=1.0 -Dpackage=de.example.shogunref -Dwebapp-name=shogunref

then patched. Nothing in shogun-core itself is changed; every behaviour the
hidden tests check is the library's.

The archetype is out of date with the library at this snapshot, so:

1. `pom.xml`: the dependency `de.terrestris:shogun-core` (the parent pom) is
   `shogun-core-main` (the jar).
2. Four generated classes had `{package}.x.Y;` instead of `import ...x.Y;` (an
   archetype template escape that no longer renders); fixed to imports.
3. `ProjectContentInitializer` and `ProjectApplicationPermissionEvaluator` used a
   `LOG` field the library no longer has; each now declares its own logger.

For r8:

4. PostgreSQL instead of H2 (Rust has no H2 driver): the
   `org.postgresql:postgresql` 42.4.3 dependency (the version the parent pom
   manages), `hikari.dataSourceClassName=org.postgresql.ds.PGSimpleDataSource`,
   `hibernate.dialect=de.terrestris.shoguncore.hibernate.ShogunPostgresqlDialect`
   (the library's own), and `jdbc.url`/`username`/`password` from `R8_JDBC_URL`,
   `R8_DB_USER`, `R8_DB_PASSWORD` (defaults: the sandbox's `aidb`, user `ai`).
5. REST security: the archetype's "demo scenario" lets ROLE_USER reach only
   `/rest/users` and keeps everything else for ROLE_ADMIN. For the slice
   (users, groups, roles, layers, layerdatasources, layerappearances) every
   user may call the endpoints and the library's entity permission evaluators
   decide, so permissions are exercised on every entity type of the slice.
6. Hibernate's second-level cache off: the Spring context set a cache region
   factory but never passed `hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache`, so
   Hibernate's default (on) applied and entities were served from memory after
   the hidden tests had reset the database with SQL. Caching is not part of
   the contract (a port has none); with it off, every request reads the
   database.

Run (Java 8, port 8081):

    R8_JDBC_URL=jdbc:postgresql://host:5432/db mvn -DskipTests jetty:run   (add -o once its dependencies are local)

`hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create`: every start drops and recreates the schema
and the archetype's initial content (users admin/shogun and user/shogun,
roles ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_USER, two groups, two OSM layers).

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans:beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/security"
       xmlns:beans="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans"
       xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans/spring-beans.xsd
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/security
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/security/spring-security.xsd">

    <!-- Authentication Manager -->
    <authentication-manager alias="authenticationManager">
        <authentication-provider ref="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" />
    </authentication-manager>

    <beans:bean id="basicAuthEntryPoint" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationEntryPoint">
        <beans:property name="realmName" value="SHOGun Realm" />
    </beans:bean>

    <beans:bean id="basicAuthenticationFilter" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationFilter">
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="authenticationManager"/>
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" />
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- (Additional) Basic auth security for REST -->
    <http auto-config='false' entry-point-ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" pattern="/rest/**" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">
        <!-- Demo scenario: users will only get access to the /rest/users interface -->
        <!-- r8: the slice is open to every user; entity permissions decide -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>

        <!-- All other interfaces can only be accessed by admins -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.superAdminRoleName}')"/>
        <custom-filter ref="basicAuthenticationFilter" before="FORM_LOGIN_FILTER"/>
        <csrf disabled="true"/>
    </http>

    <!-- Web/URL security -->
    <http auto-config="true" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">

        <logout logout-url="/logout" />

        <!-- As CSRF protection is enabled by default in Spring Security 4,
             the logout-url will only work with POST requests. To work with
             GET requests CSRF has to be disabled -->
        <csrf disabled="false"/>

        <!-- URL security -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/login/**" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/register.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/activate.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/resetPassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/changePassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')" />

    </http>

    <!-- Enables Method Security and Expression-based access control -->
    <global-method-security pre-post-annotations="enabled">
        <!-- Enables custom expression handler -->
        <expression-handler ref="methodExpressionHandler" />
    </global-method-security>

    <!-- BEANS -->

    <!-- bcrypt password encoder -->
    <beans:bean id="bcryptEncoder" class="org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder">
        <!-- Configure the strength (log rounds). Default = 10 -->
        <beans:constructor-arg value="10"/>
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- Custom Authentication Provider -->
    <beans:bean id="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.ShogunCoreAuthenticationProvider">
        <beans:property name="passwordEncoder" ref="bcryptEncoder" />
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- This bean is referenced by the http security config to assure that the role hierarchy will be used -->
    <beans:bean id="accessDecisionManager" class="org.springframework.security.access.vote.AffirmativeBased">
        <beans:constructor-arg>
            <beans:bean id="webExpressionVoter" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.WebExpressionVoter">
                <beans:property name = "expressionHandler">
                    <beans:bean id="webExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.DefaultWebSecurityExpressionHandler">
                        <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy" />
                    </beans:bean>
                </beans:property>
            </beans:bean>
        </beans:constructor-arg>
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- See http://goo.gl/o42k1S -->
    <beans:bean id="methodExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.access.expression.method.DefaultMethodSecurityExpressionHandler">
    <!-- To use hasPermission() in expressions, configure a PermissionEvaluator -->
         <beans:property name = "permissionEvaluator" ref="permissionEvaluator" />
         <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy"/>
    </beans:bean>

    <beans:bean id="permissionEvaluator" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.access.ShogunCorePermissionEvaluator">
        <beans:property name="permissionEvaluatorFactory">
            <!-- This is how project specific permission evaluators can be used/configured -->
            <beans:bean class="de.example.shogunref.security.access.factory.ProjectEntityPermissionEvaluatorFactory" />
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- http://static.springsource.org/spring-security/site/docs/3.0.x/apidocs/org/springframework/security/access/hierarchicalroles/RoleHierarchyImpl.html -->
    <beans:bean id="roleHierarchy"  class="org.springframework.security.access.hierarchicalroles.RoleHierarchyImpl">
        <beans:property name="hierarchy">
            <beans:value>
                ${role.superAdminRoleName} > ${role.defaultUserRoleName}
            </beans:value>
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>

</beans:beans>

        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>

        <!-- All other interfaces can only be accessed by admins -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.superAdminRoleName}')"/>
        <custom-filter ref="basicAuthenticationFilter" before="FORM_LOGIN_FILTER"/>
        <csrf disabled="true"/>
    </http>

    <!-- Web/URL security -->
    <http auto-config="true" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">

        <logout logout-url="/logout" />

        <!-- As CSRF protection is enabled by default in Spring Security 4,
             the logout-url will only work with POST requests. To work with
             GET requests CSRF has to be disabled -->
        <csrf disabled="false"/>

        <!-- URL security -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/login/**" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/register.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/activate.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/resetPassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/changePassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')" />

    </http>

    <!-- Enables Method Security and Expression-based access control -->
    <global-method-security pre-post-annotations="enabled">
        <!-- Enables custom expression handler -->
        <expression-handler ref="methodExpressionHandler" />
    </global-method-security>

    <!-- BEANS -->

    <!-- bcrypt password encoder -->
    <beans:bean id="bcryptEncoder" class="org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder">
        <!-- Configure the strength (log rounds). Default = 10 -->
        <beans:constructor-arg value="10"/>
    </beans:bean>

    <!-- Custom Authentication Provider -->
    <beans:bean id="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.ShogunCoreAuthenticationProvider">
        <beans:property name="passwordEncoder" ref="bcryptEncoder" />
    </beans:bean>

    <beans:bean id="accessDecisionManager" class="org.springframework.security.access.vote.AffirmativeBased">

         <beans:property name = "permissionEvaluator" ref="permissionEvaluator" />

content.text:
Several results are surprising, so I'll record them precisely:

- `output:only` returns transient objects where unprojected primitives are `false`, unprojected collections are `[]`, and everything else is `null`.
- Projecting `layerdatasources` fails with a 500 because the abstract class can't be instantiated.
- Invalid filter values seem to fall back to `0`/`false` rather than erroring.

Next I'll check how associations behave when projected, and how filter conversion treats invalid numbers.

input.content:
# Behaviour notes (reference = Java app on :8081, DB `ref`; port DB = `port`)

Seed snapshot of the reference DB: /tmp/ref_seed.dump; reset with /work/harness/reset_ref.sh.

## Auth / routing
- Basic auth on /rest/**; bad/missing/inactive/no-authority user -> 401 (WWW-Authenticate Basic realm "SHOGun Realm").
- Authorities = users_roles roles + roles of user_usergroup groups. ROLE_ADMIN > ROLE_USER (admin implies user).
- Slice paths (/rest/users|groups|roles|layers|layerdatasources|layerappearances, incl. sub paths) need ROLE_USER -> else 403.
- Other /rest/** paths need ROLE_ADMIN -> 403 for others; admin gets 404 for unknown.
- Trailing slash accepted. Wrong method -> 405. Non-int id -> 400 (after auth/405/406 checks).
- Accept header without application/json, application/*, */* -> 406 (GET/POST/PUT only).
- CSRF disabled.

## Permissions
- Factory: User -> self READ; UserGroup -> member READ; Role, LayerAppearance, LayerDataSource* -> READ for all; Layer generic.
- Generic: userpermissions(entity_id, key=user, pc) / grouppermissions; ADMIN grants all; group perms apply when user is member.
- Super admin (ROLE_ADMIN) bypasses everything.
- GET list / filter: PostFilter READ. GET id: READ else 404. PUT: READ else 404; UPDATE else 404. DELETE: READ then DELETE else 404.
- POST: non-super always 400 (new entity has no perms).
- /users/{id}/userGroups: user must exist (404), groups filtered by READ. /groups/{id}/users: group must exist, members filtered by READ(user).

## output:only
- Restrictable fields = primitive/wrapper/String fields of the class hierarchy (associations ignored; no valid -> no restriction).
- Restricted object = new X() defaults + projected fields. Non-super: only Role/LayerAppearance survive PostFilter (others have empty perms).
- LayerDataSource + output:only: 500 if any row matched, else [].

## Filter (/filter)
- Keys case-insensitive, unknown keys ignored; no valid key -> []. Values OR per key, AND across keys.
- Conversion like BeanUtils: int invalid -> 0; double invalid -> 0.0; bool: true/yes/y/on/1 vs false/no/n/off/0, else false.

## Writes
- ids: hibernate_sequences 'default', next_val+1 then store (separate tx).
- POST: body must be object else 400; unknown property -> 400; id must be null; non-super 400.
- PUT: body unparsable -> 404; empty/array/no id -> 400; id mismatch -> 400; then READ/UPDATE check (404).
  Keys applied in document order; a JSON-level error stops and the keys applied so far ARE COMMITTED, response 404.
  DB-level error (FK, etc.) -> rollback, 404.
- DELETE: 204; FK violation -> 404 (rolled back).

content.text:
The first run is informative. The failures show three real differences, and the rest pass:

1. **Filter key choice:** when a parameter name appears twice in different cases (`id` and `Id`), the Java code only uses the first key in query order.
2. **Set de-duplication:** Java's `Set<Role>` drops equal JSON-built objects (same class, name and description, `created` in the same millisecond). So `roles: [{id:1},{id:2}]` keeps one entry, and that is what the reference stores.
3. **Identity-info objects:** a `userGroups` object without an `id` is a Jackson error before any row is allocated, and my code allocated an ID for it.

I'll also fix the harness setup ordering. I'll make these changes now.

content.text:
The run shows 44 of the scenarios matching and two real differences, plus one harness setup error:

1. **Nested cascade into a loaded row (PUT `layers/16` with `appearance: {id: 14}`):** the reference returns 404 and rolls back. The loaded appearance is already in the Hibernate session, so saving a second detached instance with the same ID throws `NonUniqueObjectException`. The same applies to a loaded tile grid and its extent. A POST has nothing loaded, so it works.
2. **Deleting a layer that sits in a map (non-super user):** `LayerService.delete` removes the layer from each map through `MapService.saveOrUpdate`, which requires UPDATE on the map. So the reference returns 404 when the user lacks that permission on the map.

I'll check how `MapService` finds the maps before changing the code.

content.text: `findMapsWithLayer` only needs READ on the layer. Each map is then saved through `MapService`, which needs UPDATE on that map, and `Map` is an always-readable `Module`. I'll add a `Map` entity kind and a delete guard on the layer resource. I'll also add the session-conflict marker for the cascaded appearance and tile-grid objects.

## Learned details (beyond the list above)
- Jackson sets are HashSets of JSON-built objects: equal ones collapse (PersistentObject.equals compares
  class, created (same millisecond), names). Roles: name+description; users: all person/account fields.

- Filter keys: Jetty parameter HashMap order (bucket of Java String hash, then insertion) picks the key used for a field.
- Indexed lists (tilegrid_resolution, xyzlayerdatasrc_resolution): loaded in idx order without the null rows, padded with nulls to max idx + 1.
- NonUniqueObjectException: a cascaded object whose id is already loaded in the session fails the flush (404, rollback).
  A new tile grid whose extent is the loaded one still allocates its id first.
- LayerService.delete: non-super users need UPDATE on every map that contains the layer.
- XYZ: extent object with only an id is accepted (FK); with other fields -> flush error. Non-empty numeric resolutions -> JSON error (404).
- Java Double serialisation prefix for XYZ resolution bytes is taken from the JDK 8 output (verified in a unit test).
EOF

content.text:
The Rust service is in `rust/` and matches the Java reference on the 75 comparison scenarios I ran. `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` both pass, and the build leaves no `target/` in `rust/`.

**What's there**
- `rust/` holds `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `src/`. It builds one binary, `shogun-rest`, which reads `DATABASE_URL` and `PORT` and binds `0.0.0.0`. It starts and answers on an empty schema-only database.
- The service covers the six slice resources, including the nested-object and sub-path endpoints. Routing, HTTP Basic login with bcrypt, role gates, entity permissions, `output:only`, `/filter` and the database writes are all rebuilt in Rust. It uses no Java.
- Nothing in the schema is changed. IDs come from `hibernate_sequences` the way Hibernate allocates them.

**How I checked it**
- `/work/harness/scenarios.py` runs 75 scenarios against the reference app (port 8081, DB `ref`) and the Rust service (port 8090, DB `port`). Each scenario starts from the same seed. It compares status codes, canonicalised JSON bodies and the slice tables afterwards.
- The last full run was 75/75. The harness is in `/work/harness`, outside the deliverable.
- Some reference behaviour is surprising, and the port reproduces it on purpose:
  - A PUT that fails part-way through its JSON still commits the fields it had already applied, and then returns 404.
  - A POSTed or PUT password is stored as plain text, so that user can't log in.
  - Some sets silently drop equal-looking JSON objects.
  - A cascade into an object already loaded in the same session fails with 404.
  - Deleting a layer that sits in a map needs UPDATE on that map.

**Choices and gaps**
- I dropped one harness case, a duplicate-role POST. The reference's result depends on whether two objects are created in the same millisecond, so it can't be reproduced reliably. The rule that usually applies is in place.
- XYZ data sources follow the reference's observed rules, which are odd. Non-empty numeric `resolutions` are refused with 404, and the stored Java-serialised bytes were checked against a JDK 8 `Double`. The task marks XYZ resolutions as unchecked, so this is a best effort.
- Successful bcrypt checks are cached in memory, keyed by a salted digest of account, stored hash and password, so authenticated requests take about 7 ms. Failures are never cached. This is a deliberate speed trade-off.
- The reference's error bodies are HTML pages, and the port returns empty bodies. Only the status codes and the success JSON are matched.
